figmaBuildPlan.tokenProfileHint: Use default enterprise-safe typography (Plus Jakarta Sans headings, Inter body). Color emotion should stay trust-authority with a dark primary hero, but keep the page light and section-led. Prioritize logo trust proof and avoid lead-magnet or form blocks because none are supported in contentMap.

sections.variantHint: dark primary hero with text-led split composition; if no product screenshot is available, use centered text block with strong background and clear CTA row
sections.notes: Use headline exactly as provided, but keep it to 36px style due to 16+ word rule. Include subheadline and supporting line. Primary CTA only. No secondary CTA because contentMap is empty. Ensure text does not overflow or get cropped. Keep hero visually compact and readable.

sections.variantHint: logo-first trust strip with dominant proof signal and customer count stat
sections.notes: Make trust logos/badges the dominant trust signal. Use the supplied trust badge copy 'Trusted by 100,000+ Businesses Globally' and a corresponding customer-count stat. Keep this immediately below hero with strong separation and minimal copy.

sections.variantHint: 4-card feature section with clean readable cards, not a nested grid inside a grid
sections.notes: Use the section label FEATURES and headline exactly. Render 4 features as a 2x2 or 4-card responsive layout on desktop, but avoid inner grids inside card content. Each feature card should have title and description with ample spacing. No placeholder icons if none provided; use text-led cards with subtle system icon area only if consistent with design system.

sections.frameName: Unlock Your Business Growth with Zoho Workplace
sections.variantHint: second feature block separated by section title and intro copy; maintain readability with consistent card sizing
sections.notes: Second feature cluster should feel like an extension, not a duplicate. Keep title and description above the cards, then present 4 features in a clean, scannable arrangement. Preserve long-form content without truncation.

sections.variantHint: integration matrix with compact category cards or grouped list chips; do not force a dense icon grid
sections.notes: The provided content is truncated at 'Automation — Zoho Flow, Zapier', so preserve only available text. Present integrations as grouped categories with concise labels. Keep this section lighter and more compact than the main features blocks.

figmaExecutionNotes: Do not add pricing, testimonials, news, or form sections because they are not supported by the input.
Keep the top strip fixed only if represented as part of the header/navigation pattern; otherwise do not introduce an unsupported sticky utility bar.
Use a full-page scrollable canvas so content continues beyond the hero immediately; do not create a hero-only mockup.
Maintain section order exactly as hero → trust → product features. No invented content blocks.
Mobile should stack all sections vertically with single-column feature presentation and strong whitespace for long descriptions.
Avoid cropped images, black image blocks, or oversized hero text. The hero must remain fully legible on one screen without overflow.

heroStrategy.headline: Elevate Your Team’s Productivity with Zoho Workplace
heroStrategy.subheadline: A complete email and collaboration suite for enterprises that unifies communication, documents, meetings, and teamwork in one secure workspace.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an unexpected hero composition: a full-bleed light mesh-gradient canvas with the product UI rendered as a layered floating stack on the right-center, while the left side holds oversized copy and trust proof. Keep the hero visually airy but premium, with soft-shadow cards, orange CTA buttons, charcoal text, and thin grid-line accents. Make the visual feel operational and enterprise-ready: one large desktop workspace panel, one smaller mobile/calendar preview overlapping, plus a compact logo trust strip beneath the CTA. Use the orange brand accent only for primary actions and key highlights. Ensure H1 is 60px+ and H2 is 36px+ on the page, with at least one later section on a dark background and alternating light/dark feature sections.

repetitionBreakers: Use a split, visual-first hero to establish enterprise clarity without repeating the same card-grid rhythm.
Switch the trust section into a logo-led bar for immediate credibility.
Make the product area an accordion-with-visual so long content is scannable and not a static grid.
Use a high-density compact testimonial grid to change pace after product detail.
Finish with a centered pricing-to-CTA close to create a strong conversion endcap.
blueprint.pageTitle: Zoho Workplace for Enterprises | Unified Email and Collaboration Suite
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Zoho Workplace, an enterprise-ready email and collaboration suite with unified communication, real-time teamwork, trusted global adoption, and a simple Get Started CTA.

sections.backgroundTreatment: clean white canvas with subtle grid-line texture and light brand-red accent anchors
sections.designNote: Content-first split hero with headline continuity for warm traffic. Keep the headline direct about what Zoho Workplace is, the subheadline clearly says it is for enterprises, and the only CTA is a full-width mobile-ready solid red 'Get started'. Right side should show a bright product UI montage with mail, chat, docs, and calendar panels plus floating trust chips like Easy Setup, 24x7 Support, and Made in India. This section should feel dynamic and immediately answer what it is, who it is for, and what to do next.

Use 3-6 recognizable enterprise/customer logos in a compact flex-wrap grid. If exact logos are unavailable, convert this into a logo-style proof strip with the strongest available brand marks rather than a metrics-only block. Keep it visually prominent and early because trust strategy is logos-first. Add a short label like 'Trusted by 100,000+ businesses globally' above the logos, but avoid turning it into a generic badge wall.

Insert a 3-step, under-60-second process section immediately after trust to match the warm-traffic sequence. Use alternating split panels rather than a flat step grid: 01 Choose your plan, 02 Set up email and collaboration tools, 03 Invite teams and start working. Keep copy tight and operational. Show a small preview panel or mini workflow graphic on one side and the step list on the other. This section should feel practical, fast, and enterprise-safe.

Combine the multiple productSections into one long product block with alternating visual treatments so it does not feel generic. Because there are many features, use an accordion-with-visual pattern instead of a static card grid. Lead with the click-driving features first: unified workspace and real-time collaboration, then fold in remote access, AI productivity, integrations, and customization. Within the accordion, use a preview panel that changes context as each item expands. Keep the rhythm alternating between text-heavy and visual-heavy subgroups so adjacent content does not repeat the same layout energy.

Turn the available proof into a crisp credibility section rather than a generic testimonial dump. Use the strongest numeric proof plus 2-4 short outcome-oriented quotes or callouts, but keep the visual light because the primary proof asset here is logos and adoption scale. If customer logos are already prominent, make this section a compact industry-proof summary with a metric strip and a few quoted outcomes like streamlined communication, improved productivity, and easier remote work. Use a different visual pattern from the product accordion to break rhythm.

Create a focused section that spotlights the 1-2 features most likely to have driven the click: AI productivity and unified collaboration. Use one large spotlight panel with a supporting mini-grid of related benefits like real-time editing, anywhere access, and seamless communication. This is the third visually expressive section and should feel sharper, more editorial, and more product-specific than the earlier process or proof sections.

Present a single highlighted enterprise plan card with a strong value frame and a short included-items list. Keep it clean, centered, and easy to scan. The CTA on the card must be 'Get started' and use the accent color at full opacity. This section should feel decisive rather than comparative, since the goal is to move warm visitors toward action rather than overwhelm them with plan choice.

Use a compact 3-card testimonial grid because there are 5 quotes available and this keeps the page credible without becoming too long. Prioritize operational outcomes and implementation confidence. Keep card styling slightly elevated with soft shadows and minimal framing. Alternate quote lengths so the block feels human and not overly templated. Avoid carousel unless space becomes constrained.

Finish with a strong conversion-focused close: a centered floating card with a concise value reminder and one primary CTA only, labeled 'Get started'. Since the CTA aggression is moderate-to-strong for warm traffic, this should be the final conversion block and visually the strongest ending element. Keep it uncluttered, with full-width mobile CTA styling and no secondary action.

Only use this section if additional recognizable logos or press marks are available; otherwise omit it and keep the page tighter. Do not use a marquee unless explicitly required. If present, render it as a static horizontal logo strip with subtle labels such as integrations or compatible ecosystem brands, not as moving content.

blueprint.designPersonality: Trusted enterprise workspace: crisp, efficient, and high-clarity. The page should feel like a serious productivity platform backed by strong proof, with logo-first trust, clear CTA hierarchy, compact but premium spacing, and light surfaces that signal ease of adoption.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a clean product UI composition with overlapping workspace panels: mail inbox, chat threads, docs, and calendar previews. Add small floating trust chips around the visual for 'Easy Setup', '24x7 Support', and 'Made in India'. Keep the look bright, structured, and enterprise-focused, with no heavy dark treatment.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is moderately long, so 56px preserves impact without over-wrapping on desktop.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-column above-the-fold hero with brand logo, large left-aligned headline, short supporting paragraph, and a compact benefit list using check icons. Visual emphasis comes from typography and spacing rather than illustration-heavy composition.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Long-form landing page with stacked sections in a linear scroll. Intro hero is followed by a form block and then feature sections that repeat a consistent headline + description + grid/card pattern.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple utility cards with minimal ornamentation, light borders or subtle separation, and small icon-leading rows where needed. Cards prioritize readable text and modular content blocks over heavy imagery.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary conversion is centered on a single dominant CTA in the hero and a repeated lead-form submission flow below. Secondary CTAs are absent or de-emphasized, favoring one clear action per section.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No visible pricing module in the provided structure; the page is conversion-led via inquiry/trial form rather than package comparison.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer not represented in the provided reference structure; likely standard informational footer if present, but not a core pattern in this extract.
spacingScale: wide vertical separation between major blocks
full-width container with nested grid gutters
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Primarily text-first layout with minimal media dependence. When present, media appears as logo/brand imagery rather than large product screenshots or video panels.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Repeated feature sections use a small label kicker, large section headline, short supporting description, then a multi-column feature grid. This pattern supports long content volumes and scalable feature inventories.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead-capture form block placed directly after the hero, presented as a card-like container with clear heading and stacked fields. Hidden fields suggest tracked submission context and campaign metadata.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No explicit motion system is evidenced in the provided structure; interaction appears static and form-driven rather than animated.
designNotes: Optimize for enterprise lead generation with a clear hero-to-form conversion path.
Use a restrained visual hierarchy: logo, headline, proof points, then form, then features.
Keep section templates repeatable for long content without requiring varied media assets.
Favor readable typography, strong spacing, and simple grids over decorative UI patterns.
Maintain a utilitarian, trust-oriented tone through structured content and minimal distractions.

blueprint.heroFormBgRule: MANDATORY: Use heroBackgroundVideo as full-bleed autoplay muted loop video behind everything

mustHaveMoments: Above-the-fold hero with a concise value proposition and one primary CTA
Dominant logo/social-proof band immediately after hero to establish enterprise credibility
Readable, non-grid feature storytelling with clear section breaks and strong headings
Pricing/inclusion section that clarifies what enterprise buyers receive
Testimonial block that reinforces adoption, productivity, and procurement confidence
Persistent top CTA strip and visible footer for full-page completion and conversion access
avoidPatterns: Overextended hero copy or cluttered headline treatments
Cropped, black, or visually broken hero imagery
Lead magnets or unnecessary secondary offers
Grid-inside-grid feature layouts that reduce readability
Hero-only pages that fail to load or reveal the full scroll experience
Adding a form when the page does not require one
Content mismatch between sections and the supplied product narrative
designStrategy.reasoning: This is an enterprise landing page for a single product with a long content map, so the page should prioritize lead generation through trust and clarity rather than exploration. The strongest proof signal is logos and business scale, so trust should be led by brand credibility and reinforced with stats/testimonials. The audience is solution-aware, meaning they already understand the category and need a clear, enterprise-safe case for adoption. A split hero keeps the message prominent without overcrowding the fold, while balanced section density supports long-form scrolling without fatigue. The page should feel confident and efficient, with a proof-led narrative that moves from trust to value to features to pricing and social validation.
